ejhusom.not_measurable_reason: 5 rows x 2 columns gives 5 pairwise comparisons, so accuracy takes only the 6 values 0/20/40/60/80/100 and the finest resolvable difference is 20 points. The interaction has one degree of freedom per row (v is a 2-vector fixed up to sign and scale), so a rank-1 term has nothing to estimate beyond a single sign.

llm-perf.note: leave-one-model-out; parameter count parsed from the model identifier for 72/74 rows, median imputed elsewhere

not_attempted.llm-perf: three GPUs; holding one out leaves two training points for a two-feature regression, which is exactly determined.

diagnosis.grid5000 (workload cold start): FAILS: 85.0 against a held-out ceiling of 88.2. Root cause is not the absence of an interaction: the training residual is 61% rank-1 on average, and the same rank-1 form given the true loading scores 88.4. The cause is that the corpus has FIVE workload rows, so leave-one-workload-out fits the loading regression on FOUR points with five descriptors; RidgeCV chose the largest penalty on the grid in 3 of 5 folds, shrinking the predicted loading to zero, and in the one fold where it did not, it predicted the loading with the wrong sign and six times its true magnitude. Five workloads cannot support workload cold start. This corpus's value is its EIGHTEEN machines, and the machine cold start below is where it is used.
diagnosis.c4-training: FAILS: 85.2 against a held-out ceiling of 87.6. Same mechanism at a milder scale: 14 training rows across 5 families, and RidgeCV shrank the loading to the grid maximum in 3 of 5 folds. The interaction is present (oracle loading 91.5, 4 percentage points above the ceiling), so what fails is the descriptor regression, not the model form. c1-extended, the same accelerators with 30 rows instead of 18, does gain (+2.4), which is consistent with a sample-size cause.
diagnosis.llm-perf: NO GAIN, exactly zero: 95.5 for both the additive model and the bilinear one. The descriptors this corpus carries are the quantisation scheme and a parameter count parsed from the model identifier, and the fitted loading is driven almost entirely by the quantisation one-hot: it takes about three distinct values, so the interaction term applies a per-scheme column shift that is smaller than the machine main effect and flips no pair. The interaction itself is real and predictable in principle: the residual is 93% rank-1 and the oracle-loading model reaches 96.8. What is missing is a workload descriptor that varies WITHIN a quantisation scheme, which this corpus does not record.
diagnosis.ejhusom: 5 rows x 2 columns gives 5 pairwise comparisons, so accuracy takes only the 6 values 0/20/40/60/80/100 and the finest resolvable difference is 20 points. The interaction has one degree of freedom per row (v is a 2-vector fixed up to sign and scale), so a rank-1 term has nothing to estimate beyond a single sign.
diagnosis.grid5000 machine cold start, interaction: The bilinear term adds +0.1 points over the additive spec-prior model on the spec-only descriptor set and +0.4 with the idle probe added. The c_j regression carries the cold start (leave-one-machine-out R2 +0.59 on specs, +0.91 with the idle probe), while the v_j regression is only weakly identified (Pearson +0.54). The honest reading is that on this corpus procurement-grade descriptors place a never-measured cluster in the ranking mainly through its LEVEL, not its interaction.

protocol.model: y(i,j) = mu + r(x_i) + c_j + <w,x_i> v_j, rank-1 inductive interaction
protocol.fit: alternating additive fit, RidgeCV(logspace(-3,3,25)) for r(x) and <w,x>, v from the leading right singular vector of the training residual
protocol.splits: leave-one-workload-family-out; cold start holds out an entire machine column
protocol.ceiling: exact optimal fixed ranking by subset dynamic program over the linear ordering problem; validated against brute force for m <= 7
protocol.metric: pairwise ranking accuracy over machine pairs within a row; energy regret of the argmin-predicted machine against the row-wise oracle
